correctness.rationale: Greedy complete-alphabet arches force length at least qk. For q>=3 a permutation-block construction meets qk and has no proper border. For binary k>=2 all length-2k universal words have a one/two-letter border, and 001(01)^{k-1} attains 2k+1 without borders. Complete localization of the surplus symbol and a direct parity-based border test prove exact enumeration 4|C_k|. Independent exhaustive binary checks to k=9 and normalized-code checks to k=14; q-ary witness checks q<=8, k<=15. Finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural intersection of subsequence universality and absence of proper borders shows an exact q=2 versus q>=3 threshold, and determines every shortest binary witness by a finite intrinsic admissibility condition. The constraint changes an otherwise linear minimum by one and the classification explains its precise combinatorial boundary, useful for constrained universal-word designs.
